clue.text: County below the fringe

definitions.meaning: a home county just south of London
the horse-drawn carriage of the song 'The ... with the Fringe on Top' sits below its fringe

explanation.surface: A county lying beneath some border region.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county; the song from the musical Oklahoma! names a carriage of the same name 'with the fringe on top', so it is below the fringe.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrey is a county of south-east England, and also a light four-wheeled carriage whose canopy has a fringe.

clue.text: A case of jumping yourself out of a job ?

definitions.text: A case of jumping yourself out of a job

parts.words: A case of jumping yourself out of a job
parts.note: you jump along inside a case, a bag, and getting the bag means being dismissed from a job

explanation.surface: Someone resigning on impulse, leaving their post of their own accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the sack' is British slang for being fired; in this sports-day event each runner jumps along inside a sack, the 'case'.
explanation.definitionFit: A school sports-day contest where runners hop along with their legs inside a bag.

clue.text: Parson to about-turn and rebuke under a sounding-board?

parts.note: Rev is the short title for a clergyman

indicators.note: turn tells us to flip the little word before it end to end

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to berate is to scold or rebuke

explanation.surface: A clergyman wheeling round to scold the congregation from beneath the pulpit canopy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' in 'about-turn' flips RE (about) to ER. A sounding-board is the canopy over a pulpit, built to throw the preacher's voice back so it echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sounding-board makes the voice echo and resound, which is what happens to sound under one.

clue.text: Measure a girl

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure of about 45 inches

explanation.surface: Taking the size of a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, as of the singer Ella Fitzgerald.

clue.text: "Not that, —— flowers, Youth sighed, 'Which rose make ours?'" (Browning)

definitions.text: "Not that, —— flowers, Youth sighed, 'Which rose make ours?'" (Browning)

parts.words: Not that, —— flowers, Youth sighed, 'Which rose make ours?'" (Browning
parts.note: a quotation with a word blanked out before 'flowers', to be filled from Browning's poem Rabbi Ben Ezra

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse about youth gathering blooms, with one word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash where the missing word goes, after 'Not that,'. The line from Rabbi Ben Ezra runs 'Not that, amassing flowers, Youth sighed...'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing participle means gathering or piling up, as youth collects the blooms.

clue.text: He's in charge of an obstinate lot

definitions.text: He's in charge of an obstinate lot

parts.words: He's in charge of an obstinate lot
parts.note: the stubborn group in his care are pack animals famed for digging their heels in

explanation.surface: A boss stuck with a stubborn team of workers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'obstinate lot' sound like awkward people; they are mules, proverbially stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver of pack mules, beasts known for stubbornness.

clue.text: R.A.D.A. transport ?

parts.note: RADA, the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, trains actors: it coaches for the stage

explanation.surface: Asking how drama students get about.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is London's famous drama school; as a 'coach' for the stage it is a play on the old horse-drawn public vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: An old horse-drawn passenger vehicle; split, it is a trainer of actors for the theatre.

clue.text: Girl hailed in U.S.

parts.note: call out to this girl with a cry of 'ho!' and you have a western American state

explanation.surface: A young woman being greeted on her arrival in America.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name followed by HO, a hail, spells IDAHO, a US state, so she is 'hailed in U.S.'.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, which with a hailing cry added becomes an American state.

clue.text: They don't pull together …

parts.note: a people notorious, in history, for squabbling factions rather than unity

explanation.surface: A team that cannot cooperate, introducing the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: This runs on into 9-down: the poet who went to aid Greek independence and urged the quarrelling factions to unite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek factions of the 1820s independence war were divided among themselves.

clue.text: … This Lord tried to get them to, though

definitions.text: … This Lord tried to get them to, though

parts.words: This Lord tried to get them to, though
parts.note: a peer and poet who died at Missolonghi trying to unite the rebels of 8-down

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a nobleman attempting to make a squabbling group cooperate.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Byron went to Greece in 1823 to support its war of independence and tried to reconcile its rival leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: The Romantic poet Lord Byron spent his last months backing the Greek fight for independence.

clue.text: Battery-charging experts

parts.note: a battery is a unit of guns, and horse soldiers made charges against such positions

explanation.surface: Technicians who recharge electrical cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battery-charging' looks electrical; here a battery is a group of artillery pieces, charged by mounted troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounted soldiers, whose classic tactic is the charge against enemy guns.

clue.text: Trouble in the Jumblies' craft

parts.note: in Edward Lear's nonsense poem the Jumblies went to sea in a sieve, so water came in

explanation.surface: Difficulties aboard a nonsense-poem boat.
explanation.walkthrough: In Edward Lear's poem 'The Jumblies' the travellers 'went to sea in a Sieve', a vessel bound to let water through.
explanation.definitionFit: Escape of water through holes, the obvious problem with a sieve for a boat.

clue.text: It's unusual for the baron to look flushed

definitions.text: for the baron to look flushed
definitions.meaning: a baron of beef, a large roasting joint, looks red inside when lightly cooked

explanation.surface: An aristocrat seldom blushes.
explanation.walkthrough: A baron of beef is a double sirloin joint; underdone meat shows pink or red, 'flushed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncommon, and also describes underdone meat that is still red in the middle.

clue.text: Where traffic is slowed and a ship let through

definitions.meaning: a narrow point on a road where vehicles back up
the narrow top through which a model ship is slipped into a glass vessel

explanation.surface: A narrow channel where road vehicles crawl and a vessel passes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship is a model one, eased into the glass through its narrow top.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrowing that holds up road flow, and the narrow upper part of a glass vessel.

clue.text: Descriptive of an old house or a new

definitions.text: Descriptive of an old house or a new

parts.words: Descriptive of an old house or a new
parts.note: the word suits a Tudor-era mansion, and the reign begun in 1952 was hailed as a new age of the same name

explanation.surface: An adjective that fits both period and modern homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' suggests a building, but it is also a royal dynasty: the first Queen of the name was a Tudor, and the 1952 accession began a 'new' age.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to the reign of either Queen Elizabeth, in building style or in era.

clue.text: Not an encyclical concerning population, despite the authorship

definitions.text: Not an encyclical concerning population, despite the authorship

parts.words: Not an encyclical concerning population, despite the authorship
parts.note: a long poem about humanity by Alexander Pope, whose surname suggests a papal letter

explanation.surface: A papal letter on population that turns out to be no such thing.
explanation.walkthrough: An encyclical is a letter from the Pope; this work on mankind is by the poet Alexander Pope, so the 'authorship' is Pope but it is not papal.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope's philosophical poem of 1733-34 on humankind's place in the universe.

clue.text: Skittle-victual

definitions.meaning: in the game of skittles the flat wooden disc thrown at the pins has this name
a food made from milk curd

explanation.surface: Food served at a skittle alley.
explanation.walkthrough: In traditional English skittles, the heavy disc thrown at the pins is called the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: The disc thrown in skittles, and a dairy food made from pressed curds.

clue.text: Keep asking, that gets one a flower

parts.note: to beg on is to keep asking
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Persistence in begging finally earns someone a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden plant grown for its bright showy blooms.

clue.text: Floored again and again!

parts.note: a building with floor after floor, rather than someone knocked down repeatedly

explanation.surface: A boxer knocked down time after time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floored' sounds like knocked over; here it means given floors, one level above another.
explanation.definitionFit: Having several levels or floors, as a tall building does.

clue.text: Weaver comes by railway with ship money

parts.note: Nick Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A weaver arrives by train carrying funds for a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ship money' is a historical tax, but here it is a loan raised on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottomry is a loan in which a vessel is pledged as security for the money advanced.

clue.text: Biblical hosts

parts.note: the Hebrew word for armies in the title 'Lord God of ...'

explanation.surface: Those who entertained guests in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosts' suggests people giving hospitality; in the Bible it means armies, as in 'the Lord of Sabaoth'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hebrew word meaning armies, kept untranslated in some Bible versions.

clue.text: No vessel company can make such a sizable return on paper

indicators.note: return asks for the joined pieces to be read from the back

parts.note: O looks like nought, nothing
a vat is a large tub or vessel

explanation.surface: A firm without ships still hopes for a handsome paper profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reads the three pieces backwards. 'sizable' leans on 'on paper': the answer is a paper or book size.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo names a page size, each sheet folded into eight leaves, so it describes how big a book is.

clue.text: Partisan remarks ?

parts.note: taken as remarks belonging to one party or faction, words murmured off to the side

explanation.surface: Biased comments from a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partisan' suggests bias; read it as remarks made to one party only, as an actor speaks quietly past the other characters on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Words spoken in an undertone, as by an actor to the audience.

clue.text: A fast disappearing craft

parts.note: a vessel that vanishes swiftly upwards beyond the sky: a rocket

explanation.surface: A traditional trade that is quickly dying out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a skill dying out; it is a vehicle, which with this word in front leaves Earth quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Space is the void beyond Earth's atmosphere; a spacecraft flies off into it and vanishes.

clue.text: In brief, Peg North's a character !

indicators.note: a character is an odd sort, so the letters before it are to be rearranged

parts.note: the S of the possessive is part of the letters here

explanation.surface: A short way of saying that a person called Peg North is an odd one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' rearranges PEG NORTHS A. 'In brief' points to shorthand writing; the answer is also the noun for a shorthand character.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorthand writing records speech in abbreviated form, briefly.

clue.text: They are of measurably long standing

definitions.text: They are of measurably long standing

parts.words: They are of measurably long standing
parts.note: what we stand on, and also a unit of length used in measuring

explanation.surface: Things that have existed for a measurable long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long standing' looks like age; read it as standing, done on these, which are also measures of length.
explanation.definitionFit: The body parts one stands on, also units of length of twelve inches each.

clue.text: For the swinging rather than the jet set it seems

definitions.text: For the swinging rather than the jet set it seems

parts.words: For the swinging rather than the jet set it seems
parts.note: a ... has swings for fun-seekers, and light hair is the opposite of jet black

explanation.surface: Something aimed at fun-lovers more than wealthy globetrotters.
explanation.walkthrough: The swinging are on swingboats at a funfair; jet is black, so light-coloured hair is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A funfair with swings, and light-coloured as opposed to jet black.

clue.text: Can get home in twenty-four hours from here

indicators.note: in places the word home inside the word for a full day

parts.note: a day lasts twenty-four hours
taken as written

explanation.surface: A place so close you can reach home within a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from here' points to a place: the old name of the West African country now called Benin.
explanation.definitionFit: The former French colony in West Africa, renamed Benin in 1975, a place one could be 'from'.

clue.text: Ayesha's possessive

parts.note: Ayesha is the title character of Rider Haggard's novel She, and the possessive form of she is wanted

explanation.surface: A woman called Ayesha being jealous.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayesha is 'She-who-must-be-obeyed' in H. Rider Haggard's novel She; 'possessive' is the grammatical form, not jealousy.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun of the feminine third person, belonging to a woman.

clue.text: Location of the Bacon Society's conversazione?

parts.note: a conversazione is a social gathering for talk, a chat
ham is cured pork, like bacon

explanation.surface: Asking where literary scholars of Francis Bacon held their gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bacon Society studies Francis Bacon; 'Bacon' here is just HAM. Chatham is a naval town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Medway in Kent, a place on the map.

clue.text: Air through a window

parts.note: a tune sung up to a lady's window, not a draught

explanation.surface: A breeze coming in from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' looks like a draught; it is a song, sung by a lover beneath a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A love song performed in the evening beneath a beloved's window.

clue.text: Formed by the fingers of " this man, with lime and roughcast "

definitions.text: Formed by the fingers of " this man, with lime and roughcast "

parts.words: Formed by the fingers of " this man, with lime and roughcast
parts.note: in A Midsummer Night's Dream the actor playing Wall makes a chink with his fingers for the lovers

explanation.surface: Something made by a plasterer's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, Snout plays Wall, 'this man, with lime and roughcast', and holds up his fingers as the chink through which Pyramus and Thisbe whisper.
explanation.definitionFit: A small gap or chink, as in a wall.
